findings.Quote: "Yes," she said.
findings.Note: Purpose requires Rook to say yes before hearing the job and to knowingly pay the cost of that habit; the beat shows the yes but the surrounding interiority (four names, Tidewell) arrives after, making the 'knows exactly what that costs' feel asserted via backfill rather than dramatized in the moment of saying it.
findings.Fix: Let a flicker of the cost register in her body at the instant of the yes, before the explanatory paragraph.

findings.Quote: Introduce Sefi Okonkwo-Reyes (a survivor with a name/face/drive): "There were twenty-one of us. I can give you nine."

findings.Fix: Add Sefi's entrance and her quoted line within this beat as specified.

findings.Quote: At the edge of Rook's sight, Vox hadn't moved since she sat down.
findings.Note: Vox has not been established as present/seated in this scene within the given beats (ref 0-2 show Rook, Soraya, Stave, and — per purpose — Sefi; Vox's arrival was described in ref 1 as a future/anticipated event, 'two hours late with coffee'), so her sudden presence here without introduction reads as inconsistent with the established roster in-scene.
findings.Fix: Either show Vox's arrival explicitly earlier or cut this reference.

findings.Quote: A man already past his own denial has nothing left to protect but the work.
findings.Note: aphoristic universal-truth summary that tells us the meaning of the scene rather than trusting the preceding image

findings.Quote: the grip that never decides whether it's holding the rail up or being held up by it
findings.Note: Purple, over-worked metaphor that doesn't survive literal scrutiny — a hand gripping a rail isn't ambiguous in this way, and the parallel to the clerk's gesture strains for meaning rather than earning it.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause; let 'she put her hand on the rail' stand alone or replace with a concrete physical detail (whitened knuckles, cold metal).

findings.Quote: For one clean second it was simple in a way it hadn't been simple in three jobs: end the woman, end the program's hand, walk the count out.
findings.Note: Purpose calls for an argument neither side can win clean — this narrates Rook's internal clarity/resolve rather than dramatizing the unwinnable moral tangle the beat promises.
findings.Fix: Complicate the beat with a flicker of what killing Anneke would cost or fail to solve, undercutting the 'clean' feeling in the same breath.

findings.Quote: His body did what bodies do: it told him in one white flood to set the weight down and step off the line.
findings.Note: 'white flood' as a shorthand for pain-signal is a stock sensory tag that doesn't add specificity beyond genre convention.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete physical detail unique to his own body-as-structure logic, e.g., describe the exact sensation his trade vocabulary would give it.

findings.Fix: Name what the care is about, e.g., 'set them down like she'd already rehearsed the next sentence.'

findings.Fix: Ensure Sefi's introduction (per ref 2) precedes this reaction so the payoff is earned.
